text:
Fixed via option 2 (ephemeral), which turned out to dominate option 1 rather than merely complement it.

The three unbounded content-addressed keys named derived selection-position domains — the active voxels of a mask, the radial active support, the dataset's active voxel set. Audit finding that decided it: NOTHING anywhere used .id, .key, .record or samePersistentIdentityAs on any of them. They were typed FiniteSpace but never used as persistable; every consumer needed only FiniteDomain capabilities (sameRuntimeOwnerAs, descriptor, pointOption, and as an argument to Selection/Region/TotalMap/IndexedField constructors, all of which take FiniteDomain).

So they are exactly what locus4s documents ephemeral for. Changes:
- DomainFactory.ephemeral / unsafeEphemeral added; SomeFiniteDomain exported from the facade.
- threshold/MaskedField: activeSpace is now FiniteDomain, built ephemerally.
- latent/RadialSelection: same for RadialMaskOrder.activeSpace.
- dataset/DatasetAcquisitionDomain: activeVoxelSpace ephemeral; time and full-voxel domains stay keyed and canonical, which is the right split — the first two are structural, the third is a selection over the second.

This beats hashing on three counts: the megabyte key string is never BUILT, not merely not retained (an O(n) allocation removed from every construction); nothing enters the registry at all; and it is collision-free, whereas a digest would have introduced a small but real chance of two different masks canonicalizing to one owner, which is precisely the unsoundness embedding avoided.

Cost, accepted: two separately built supports over identical content are now distinct owners. Correct for a derived structure — compare through the parent domain, which is canonical.

Remaining content keys are deliberately left: atlas parcels/networks (AtlasQuotient 94/145/213) and surface parcels (SurfaceLocusDomain 184) embed region id lists, but they are bounded by atlas size (hundreds, a few KB) and are genuinely semantic domains that should canonicalize — two loads of the same parcellation ought to be one domain.

Pinned by DomainIdentityProbeSuite: 50 ephemeral supports leave registeredCount unchanged, carry no persistentRecord/persistentKey, and are distinct owners.

Verified: testAll 80 suites, 4355 tests, 0 failures, JVM and Scala.js.
